description: List the open tasks of a saved `fallow mutation` JSON report as one batch (default: the report that the last run saved in the Fallow cache). A task is a survived or no_coverage mutant: a small change to the code that no test detected. Each task has the mutant_id, file, line, function, operator, status, the source lines before and after the change (original_lines, mutated_lines), and the covering test files. After `fallow mutation --record-args values`, a task can have witness; only witness.verdict witness gives a test input (args, original, mutant), and a verdict is never equivalent; see fallow://tools/mutation_tasks. Write tests that pass on the current code and fail on the changed code; one test can cover several tasks, and a task that no input can detect can be skipped. A task whose file changed after the report is stale and has no code. This tool never runs tests. A report needs the CLI command `fallow mutation`, which executes the project's tests, so ask your host first. A Rust root is not supported yet.

allow_remote_extends.description:
Allow trusted HTTPS config `extends` for this request. Used only
without `report`, as for `config`. Defaults to false and never grants
process-global trust.

config.description:
Path to a fallow config file. Used only without `report`, to find the
cache directory that holds the report of the last run.

report.description:
Path to a saved `fallow mutation --format json` report. A relative
path resolves against `root`. Without `root`, it resolves against the
working directory of the MCP server. Omitted: the report that the last
`fallow mutation` run saved in the Fallow cache of the project.

root.description: Project root; defaults to the working directory.

name: mutation_tasks
